title: Move a point, move the border
hook: Nobody draws a nearest-neighbour border. So where does it come from?

knows: that nearest-neighbour labels a new point by its closest training example
midpoints and distances on a plane
doesNotKnow: that a decision boundary is built from the training points
where a nearest-neighbour border lies between two points

misconception: Moving one training point changes only that point's label, not the boundary.
objective: The learner can explain that a one-nearest-neighbour border lies where two opposing points are equally far away (halfway between them, at right angles to the line joining them), so moving a training point moves the decision for the whole region around it.

claims.text: With A at x = 0 and B at x = 4 the one-nearest-neighbour border is at x = 2; with A at x = -2 it is at x = 1, halfway between. A moved 2 and the border moved 1.
claims.source: On the axis the border is the midpoint: (0 + 4)/2 = 2, (-2 + 4)/2 = 1. Reproduced by axisCrossing() in Demo.tsx.

claims.text: In two dimensions the border between two points is the line through their midpoint at right angles to the line joining them, so lifting A off the axis tilts it.
claims.source: |q - A|² = |q - B|²  ⟺  2(B - A)·q = |B|² - |A|², a line perpendicular to B - A through (A + B)/2. Implemented by sideOfA() in Demo.tsx; the axis crossing is (16 - ax² - ay²) / (2(4 - ax)).

claims.text: With many points, a nearest-neighbour border is stitched from such pieces.
claims.source: 1-NN decision regions are unions of Voronoi cells, whose edges lie on perpendicular bisectors: de Berg, Cheong, van Kreveld & Overmars 2008, Computational Geometry, 3rd ed., ch. 7; Hastie, Tibshirani & Friedman 2009, §13.3.

claims.text: The toy has one training point per class: A (blue, movable) and B (orange, fixed at (4, 0)).
claims.source: The lesson's own setup in Demo.tsx (B, sliders for A from x = -4 to 0 and y = -2 to 2).

claims.text: With many points, moving any training point near a nearest-neighbour border moves the decision for every spot around it.
claims.source: Reveal paragraph 2. CONCERN from the fact-checker: in 1-NN, nudging one training point only changes the class of spots that switch nearest neighbour (the sliver between its old and new Voronoi cell); in a 6-point test, moving one point by 0.5 changed the class of only 0.8% of the plane. 'Every spot around it' overstates; suggest 'moves the decision for the spots that were closest to it' or similar. Added by fact-checker 2026-10-13; needs an independent check.

recall.question: A nearest-neighbour model separates 'spam' from 'not spam'. One spam training example near the border is deleted. What happens?
options: The border shifts, and some nearby new emails change label
Only that one example's label changes
Nothing, the border was fixed when the model was built
recall.why: A nearest-neighbour border is wherever opposing training points are equally far away. Remove or move a point near it and the border moves, changing the label of every new email in the region it sweeps.
